risk_tolerance.rationale: After the Gallipoli resignation, personally volunteered for and served in frontline trench combat in France in 1916 -- a documented instance of accepting direct physical risk following a major public political failure, in addition to the already-scored 1940 war-cabinet decision.

independent_thinking.rationale: Crossed the floor of the House of Commons twice in his career (Conservative to Liberal in 1904, back to Conservative in 1924), a specific, well-documented pattern of prioritizing his own political judgment over party loyalty in both directions.

persistence.rationale: Spent his 'wilderness years' (roughly 1929-1939) marginalized from government, documented as repeatedly and publicly warning about Nazi German rearmament while largely disbelieved by the political mainstream, sustained for a full decade before events proved him correct.

achievement_drive.rationale: ERROR_CORRECTION (post-PR28-review factual correction, 2026-09): After leaving office, wrote a six-volume history of The Second World War; in 1953 he received the Nobel Prize in Literature for his mastery of historical and biographical description as well as his brilliant oratory in defending exalted human values -- the prize recognized his broader literary/historical work, not the WWII history specifically. A specific, documented sustained achievement distinct from his political career.

cross_domain_range.rationale: Documented sustained output across soldiering (Sudan, South Africa), journalism (war correspondent), multi-decade high-office politics, and published history/memoir writing across a 60+ year public career, inferred from the documented breadth of his career record.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: After the 1915 Gallipoli campaign failure, was forced to resign as First Lord of the Admiralty and became the campaign's principal public scapegoat despite documented shared responsibility across the war cabinet; publicly defended his own decisions in the House of Commons on 15 November 1915 rather than quietly stepping aside -- a specific, dated instance of sustaining a public, high-stakes defense of a contested decision.

decisiveness.rationale: Resigned his government position entirely in November 1915 rather than accept a token consolation post (Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster) he judged inadequate, then volunteered for active frontline military service in France -- a specific, documented, immediate consequential decision following the Gallipoli failure.

curiosity.rationale: Sustained engagement across soldiering, journalism, painting (the subject of his own book 'Painting as a Pastime'), bricklaying, and history writing suggests broad underlying curiosity, inferred from the documented range of pursuits.

aesthetic_sensitivity.rationale: Took up oil painting as an adult hobby, documented well enough to be the subject of his own published essay, suggesting some real aesthetic engagement, though the depth of his personal aesthetic judgment beyond the hobby itself is less directly documented.

social_assertiveness.rationale: Sustained public political leadership through wartime broadcasts and parliamentary speeches implies strong social assertiveness, inferred from the documented centrality of his public communication role.

leadership_drive.rationale: A 60-year career consistently oriented toward the highest offices of government implies strong underlying leadership drive, inferred from the documented career trajectory rather than a single stated ambition.

adaptability.rationale: Successfully returning to high office in 1951 (as Prime Minister a second time) after his 1945 electoral defeat suggests real political adaptability, inferred from the documented career recovery.

discipline.rationale: Sustained wartime working hours documented in multiple biographies (chairing late-night meetings, extensive dictation of memoranda) suggest real behavioral discipline under sustained pressure, inferred rather than measured directly.

detail_orientation.rationale: Documented practice of personally reviewing and annotating extensive military and intelligence reports during WWII suggests real attention to detail, inferred from the documented volume of his own wartime paperwork.

creative_originality.rationale: His WWII memoir's synthesis of personal narrative with historical analysis was distinctive for its genre, suggesting real creative approach to the writing itself, inferred rather than critically assessed here in depth.

mastery_orientation.rationale: Sustained, increasingly sophisticated political and literary output across six decades suggests developing mastery, inferred from the documented career arc.

collaboration.rationale: Sustained wartime alliance management (with Roosevelt, Stalin, and the war cabinet) implies real collaborative capacity at the highest level, inferred from the documented functioning of the wartime alliance.

proactive_agency.rationale: Repeatedly initiating and sustaining unpopular political positions (rearmament warnings, wartime resolve) beyond what his formal role required at the time suggests real self-initiated agency, inferred from the documented pattern.

autonomy_need.rationale: The repeated pattern of breaking with his own party over matters of principle suggests real independence orientation, inferred from the documented floor-crossing pattern already noted above under independent_thinking.

analytical_rigor.rationale: His early, specific, and ultimately accurate warnings about German rearmament (contrasted with the prevailing political consensus) suggest real analytical capability, inferred from the documented accuracy of his assessment relative to consensus.

provenance.notes: Session 7 source-first workflow: identity/QID verified, source richness assessed and confirmed BEFORE any trait scoring began -- rows below were scored only after a genuine evidence base of several distinct, specific, dated documented episodes was established, not filled in mechanically to hit an attribute-count target. inclusion_v1: passes -- while born into an aristocratic family (his father was a prominent MP, his grandfather a duke), the political/literary achievements the roster credits him for (WWII leadership, the Nobel Prize in Literature) are his own, individually attributed accomplishments, not exercises of an inherited title or office; the counterfactual test (would these specific achievements still be notable without the inherited position) is satisfied -- his own multi-decade political career, built and rebuilt through electoral politics rather than inherited office, is the clearest evidence of this. Roster28 fast-batch audit (2026-09): mechanical row scan found no extremity violations. risk_tolerance (90) and independent_thinking (88) each cite two genuinely distinct dated episodes (1916 frontline service + 1940 war-cabinet decision; 1904 and 1924 floor-crossings) -- multi-instance, not a violation. persistence (85, the 1929-1939 'wilderness years') describes a sustained pattern of repeated public warnings over a decade, not a single anecdote or one continuous undertaking -- checked against scoring-rubric-v1 Section 4 and kept as a defensible extreme score for a trait this central to how Churchill is understood historically. Held only on eligibility_v2's confidence/coverage floors (avgConf 0.509 vs 0.55, coverage 0.599 vs 0.6 -- essentially at the boundary) -- existing evidence is publication-auditable; moved to evidence_approved. Eligibility-only holdReason removed. Post-PR28-review ERROR_CORRECTION (2026-09): achievement_drive's rationale inaccurately implied the 1953 Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded specifically for the six-volume WWII history; corrected to the actual citation (mastery of historical/biographical description and oratory). No score/confidence/evidenceType/impact change -- he still wrote the history and still received the prize; only the causal attribution was imprecise.
